turns.assessment: Both endpoints switched svc017 from working to protection at essentially the same time, while every neighbouring service—including unprotected svc232 on the same nominal S11-S21-S24 route—remained healthy. This strongly localizes the problem to svc017's working ODU or endpoint-specific equipment rather than shared optical plant, amplifiers, ROADMs, or an S21 switch-fabric failure. The observations do not distinguish an ODU cross-connect defect from either endpoint port, and none of the documented modes cleanly explains a newly occurring brief, service-specific event, so commitment is unsafe.

proposals.rationale: A defect confined to svc017's working ODU can cause protection activation without optical changes or impact to services sharing the route. However, a hard misconnect normally follows provisioning and is not inherently transient.

A service-specific endpoint failure is compatible with the absence of optical and neighbouring-service effects, but the symmetric protection switches do not identify S11 and a client failure may also affect the protection copy.
This has the same service-local explanation as the S11 port, but the evidence is symmetric and cannot select S24.
A channel-specific filter penalty could disrupt a working lightpath without changing power, but unchanged quality monitoring and unaffected route neighbours argue against it.

Receiver-local degradation could trigger a service-path defect while optical power remains normal, but the simultaneous indications at both service endpoints and lack of receiver quality changes make it weak.
